title: Extrapolation must look beyond pretraining
subtitle: Hinted scaling · Muon fine-tuning reversal · Self-distillation versus GRPO · EDM
intro: Three main readings and three briefs: hints reveal curves beneath near-zero accuracy, data scale changes fine-tuning frontiers, and new skills must be evaluated alongside forgetting. The EDM classic separates denoising, preconditioning and numerical sampling.

articles.authors: Suze van Adrichem · Luke Bailey · Rohith Kuditipudi · Christine Ye · Neil Band · Ahmed Ahmed · John Duchi · Percy Liang · Tatsunori Hashimoto
articles.title: When small models fail, make the task easier first
articles.evidence: Read v1 sections 2–4: hints, fitting and extrapolation experiments; not reproduced

blocks.text: Near-zero small-model accuracy hides extrapolation signals. The authors introduce a difficulty axis H through truncated/masked reference solutions or teacher-logit mixing, then extrapolate to the unhinted task H=0.[1]

blocks.label: Empirical fit; C is log₁₀ FLOPs, or log₁₀ parameter count for post-trained families—not raw compute [1]

blocks.tex: s_H=z_{\rm model}+H z_{\rm teacher},\qquad y_t\sim\operatorname{softmax}(s_H/T),\qquad \widehat L=L(C_{\rm large},0)
blocks.label: Logit hint: teacher sees a reference solution and shares the tokenizer; F is the floor, l/A are sigmoid asymptotes, and β are fitted coefficients [1]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: This is empirical extrapolation with reference solutions and additional evaluation cost. Success across tested tasks does not guarantee transfer to arbitrary families, hints or larger scales.[1]

articles.paper: Pretraining Data Scale Reverses the Muon–AdamW Fine-Tuning Gap
articles.authors: Catherine Li · Jingchu Gai · Andrej Risteski · Jacob Mitchell Springer · Aditi Raghunathan
articles.title: Lower pretraining loss need not yield a better fine-tuning frontier
articles.evidence: Read v1 section 3 experiments and section 4 associative-memory model; proof not fully checked; not reproduced

blocks.text: OLMo-style models of 30M–600M parameters, pretrained on 150M–154B DCLM tokens, are compared on new-task loss versus pretraining forgetting. Increasing data can reverse Muon’s advantage under both checkpoint-selection protocols.[2]

blocks.tex: \operatorname{TPR}=D/N,\qquad \Delta\mathcal L_{\rm PT}=\mathcal L_{\rm PT}(\theta_{\rm FT})-\mathcal L_{\rm PT}(\theta_{\rm PT})
blocks.label: D denotes pretraining tokens, N parameters; the frontier measures fine-tuning loss and forgetting jointly [2]
Paper margin–spread ratio: mean margins alone do not determine robustness; their dispersion also matters [2]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Crossover points depend on the task. Theory uses Gaussian keys/values, zero initialization and one full-batch GD versus exact-polar Muon step in a linear model—not a general AdamW or nonlinear-LLM theorem.[2]

articles.paper: Learning new skills without forgetting: Self-Distillation vs GRPO
articles.title: Student-generated rollouts can still forget
articles.evidence: Read methods, sequential/mixed training, lenient-format evaluation and appendix setup; not reproduced

blocks.text: Full-weight Nemotron Nano 9B training, with thinking off in the main experiment, proceeds through tool use → science → Knights & Knaves. Self-distillation matches token distributions to a demonstration-conditioned teacher on student rollouts; GRPO uses verifiable rewards.[3]

blocks.tex: p_S(\cdot\mid x,y_{<t})\longleftrightarrow p_T(\cdot\mid x,d,y_{<t}),\qquad \Delta R_j=R_j(\theta_{\rm final})-R_j(\theta_{\rm base})
blocks.label: Mechanism schematic: d is a demonstration; ΔR measures each retained capability j; no KL direction is asserted

blocks.text: Mixed training reduces self-distillation’s logic-theme drop from about 30 to 4 pp. Even lenient formatting leaves a 37-pp BBH logic decline, so formatting does not explain everything.[3]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: Iterations are matched, not wall-clock time or total compute; GRPO’s multiple rollouts carry additional cost. One model/task chain does not establish universal RL superiority.[3]

articles.paper: Test-Time Scaling for Open-Ended Reasoning at Small Model Scale
articles.authors: Adam Y. Ahmed · Abdullah G. Elafifi
articles.title: Brief | More samples need not diversify open-ended answers
articles.evidence: Based on the abstract; full text not read

blocks.text: Across 250 open-ended prompts, three 2–3B model families and two generation seeds, semantic-cluster voting yields at most 0.30 judge-point gains, unlike useful mathematical voting. Judge points are not accuracy; the proposed diversity explanation needs full-text examination.[4]

articles.paper: Sparks of Weight-Space Programming: LLMs can natively read & write neural network weights
articles.authors: Rikiya Takehi · Jayden Teoh · Alex Zhang · Omar Khattab
articles.title: Brief | Editing weights: repair versus acquiring ability
articles.evidence: Read experiments 1–3, 8 and the Gemma negative result; not reproduced

blocks.text: GPT-6 Astra edits 0.016% of Qwen3.5-0.8B weights to reduce looping, raising MATH-500 from 7.9% to 48.1%, with 50 batched forward-feedback calls. Gradient-free does not mean evaluation-free. No established gain on rarely looping Gemma 270M separates removing an obstacle from adding mathematical ability.[7]

classic.authors: Tero Karras · Miika Aittala · Timo Aila · Samuli Laine
classic.title: Separate denoising, loss weighting and the solver
classic.dateNote: First posted 2022-06-01; read v2 (2022-10-11), sections 2–5 and Table 1; NeurIPS 2022
classic.evidence: Read denoising identity, preconditioning, Heun sampling and training ablations; not reproduced

recognition.label: NeurIPS 2022 Featured Paper · Official conference blog checked 2026-11-03

classic.question: For a fixed trained denoiser and equal NFE, how can we distinguish score-estimation error, noise-grid discretization and ODE-solver error?

blocks.text: DDPM (2020) and score SDEs (2021) generate by progressive denoising. EDM unifies their design space and varies sampling and training separately.[8,9]
Let y be clean data, ε∼N(0,I) independent, and pσ the noisy density. σdata parameterizes data standard deviation; exact identities and neural approximations differ.[8]

blocks.label: Under Gaussian corruption, the squared-error-optimal denoiser gives the score [8]

blocks.tex: D_\theta(x,\sigma)=c_{\rm skip}x+c_{\rm out}F_\theta(c_{\rm in}x;c_{\rm noise}),\quad c_{\rm skip}=\frac{\sigma_{\rm data}^2}{\sigma^2+\sigma_{\rm data}^2},\quad c_{\rm out}=\frac{\sigma\sigma_{\rm data}}{\sqrt{\sigma^2+\sigma_{\rm data}^2}},\quad c_{\rm in}=\frac1{\sqrt{\sigma^2+\sigma_{\rm data}^2}},\quad c_{\rm noise}=\tfrac14\log\sigma
blocks.label: Paper preconditioning controls input/target scales and retains a skip path [8]
Training configuration: λ c²out=1, but noise levels are not sampled equally often [8]
Probability-flow ODE with σ(t)=t and s(t)=1; the learned denoiser approximates D* [8]
Heun predictor–corrector; final σ=0 step uses Euler to avoid division by zero; N intervals require 2N−1 network evaluations [8]

blocks.title: Boundary
blocks.text: The identity removes neither score error nor finite-step error. Training ablations do not show that preconditioning alone must improve FID; weighting, noise sampling and augmentation need separate comparisons.[8]
